mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns during a period of declining FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the short term.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns despite rising unemployment, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) without corresponding increases in the federal funds rate may indicate inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns despite the CPI-FEDFUNDS gap, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) during an economic expansion signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth does not lead to positive S&P 500 returns, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above a certain threshold may signal supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of GDP growth (GDPC1) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) behaviors may indicate economic inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns despite the GDPC1-UNRATE pattern, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) growth during an economic expansion signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns, this hypothesis is invalid.
